newsitem.title: UK: IGC lifts coarse grains harvest, end-season stocks.
newsitem.headline: IGC lifts coarse grains harvest, end-season stocks.

text.p: The International Grains Council (IGC) raised its estimate for world coarse grains output in 1996 by 6.0 million tonnes from its previous forecast to 875 million.

It saw coarse grains stocks at the end of the 1996/97 (July/June) season at 105 million tonnes, five million higher than last month's estimate and 21 million above the 1995/96 level when stocks were at 20-year lows.
"Most of the increase is attributable to the United States," said the IGC in its latest monthly report.
But Bill De Maria, assistant executive director of the IGC, said the market was still operating with a small demand/supply margin.
"Stocks are rebuilding but it's nothing spectacular," he said.

The total U.S. harvest, mainly maize, was pegged at 260.4 million tonnes, up from last month's 255.6 million, based on official U.S. estimates which pegged the country's maize crop at 229 million tonnes due to better yields.
"Harvest weather has been good in most areas with the exception of the southeast, where heavy rains interrupted fieldwork," the IGC said.

Canada was another winner with its output now seen by the IGC at 28.5 million tonnes compared with the previous 27.5 million tonnes, and up from 24 million in 1995 mainly as a result of an increase in acreage.
But grain quality was affected by cold and wet weather at harvest time.
The IGC pegged the Australian crop, mainly barley, at 9.6 million tonnes, 1.1 million tonnes higher than projections made in September.

But it trimmed the forecasts for countries in the Former Soviet Union, with Russia pegged at 38.5 million tonnes from 39.0 million because of lower than expected yields and the Ukraine at 13.6 million tonnes from 14.7 million.
Harvesting of coarse grains had been delayed in Kazakhstan due to a severe shortage of agricultural equipment, it said.
Elsewhere, planting of maize was under way in Brazil and a larger crop was expected. Maize sowings had a good start in Argentina and a larger crop was expected.
